method: Manual visual marking from full-band, below-160-Hz, and above-2-kHz spectrogram/waveform views. Marks were rounded to the nearest 10 ms before any detector output for this window was inspected. The spectrogram used a 1024-sample window at 22050 Hz (about 46 ms), so the honest attack-time resolution is plus or minus 50 ms; the 10 ms numeric step is not a 10 ms accuracy claim.

voiceLabels.kick_or_low_drum: Abrupt low-band bloom with a clear attack edge; believed to be kick or another low drum.
voiceLabels.snare_or_clap: Broadband vertical attack with more mid/high energy than low-frequency body.
voiceLabels.hat_or_bright_attack: Brief upper-band attack with little low-frequency bloom; believed to be hat, shaker, or similar bright percussion.

matchingToleranceRationale: Deliberately larger than annotationGranularityMilliseconds. Ground truth here is accurate to about +/-50 ms, and the detector has its own error, so matching at 50 ms counts annotation noise as detector misses. It did: at a 50 ms tolerance this fixture reported 10/22 recall and an F1 of 0.33, which was read as an architecturally broken detector. At 100 ms the same detector and the same annotations give 18/22. A matching tolerance must exceed the resolution of the ground truth it matches against.
